items.title: Frank Wess — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Yeah, Ted Nash, Scott Robinson, Frank Greene, myself, Winard Harper on drums

ctx.x: Yeah I’m going in on the 19th, the week of the 19th of this month with my nonet. I got some good players.
I have the players right here. You have Ted Nash, can you mention all the players.

items.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014
items.q: I remember one time too, maybe Frank Wess told me this story and then I think Buddy Catlett confirmed it.

ctx.x: Well the answer is it’s a job for all of us, in all walks of life, whatever you do. Everybody can take it and take the fundamentals and the essence of jazz and apply it. Because sometimes you even hear stories about some of these bands — like I’ve heard somebody tell me some stories about Duke Ellington’s band saying you know nobody in that band got along. I mean I never heard, I might have to do some checking into it further, see a lot

of those guys didn’t like each other which is kind of amazing. Because if that was the case, then that too says that look, they understood that even if that was the case, you had some problem with somebody, when they got on the bandstand, that bandstand was sacred. We’re going to take care of business. We’re going to spread the love, and this is the thread that’s going to tie us all together. So that’s a great thing. Music is powerful. I remember one time too, maybe Frank Wess told me this story and then I think…
